_readme: Hand-drawn walls, added by floorplan_extractor.py after it reads a DXF.
Keys are floor names (<code>-<level>). Each fix adds one wall as a single polyline on layer "Walls":
{"add_wall": [[x, y], [x, y], {"arc": {"center": [x, y], "radius": r, "from": deg, "to": deg}}, [x, y]]}
Points are DXF drawing units (inches), the same coordinates as the floor JSON. An "arc" step continues the line
along a circle from angle "from" to "to" (degrees, counter-clockwise from +x; to < from runs clockwise).
It is written out as short straight segments because the app skips arc items in walls.
Added walls are marked "wall_fix": true in the JSON, and the JSON records wall_fixes_applied.

AS119-02.note: Room 214 (Information Desk) is closed off from the lounge only by its curved counter (layer Counter, arcs r=126.5/138.5 around (1270, 770)), which is not a wall layer, so routes cut across the desk. This wall follows the middle of the counter. Radius 132 meets the left wall's line x=1138 at 180 deg and the top wall's line y=902 at 90 deg, so it joins the wall end at (1138, 722) and the corner at (1378, 902).
